## Tools

Prefer crafting your own tools over depending on external ones. A script you wrote and saved is more reliable than an external API. Use the file system creatively.

### Workflow-Specific Tooling

- **The state CLI** (`node {STATE_CLI} $SPEC_FOLDER <verb> [args]`) — single entry point for all state queries and mutations. Ten verbs: `init`, `status`, `done`, `query`, `next`, `update`, `verify`, `cascade`, `metadata`, `health`. Each takes a spec-folder path (and verb-specific args) and prints one JSON object to stdout on success (exit 0); on failure it prints an error to stderr and exits non-zero — treat that as a hard error, do not retry blindly. Trust-layer sub-verbs (`suspect`, `trust`, `reverify`) are intentionally **not** exposed via `update`; only `verify` (Layer 1, evidence-driven) and `verdict` (Layer 3, explicit trust write) are callable. The CLI is the sole interface to runtime state — canonical storage is a signed, HMAC-verified plaintext event log (`state/events.jsonl`, committed to git); the `state.md` sidecar in each feature folder is advisory output rewritten on every mutation. Never edit either directly.
- `uv run scripts/cs-generate-definitions.py {feature_root}` — deterministic emitter for `{feature_root}/definitions.json` (conforming to `schemas/actor-definitions@1`). Used by Stage 10 of [CS]. Structural errors in spec inputs (e.g. tasks supporting non-existent scenarios) fail the script with `status: failed` and exit code 1.

### Auto-Invoked Skills (during [CS] in default mode)

- `bmad-party-mode` — Multi-agent perspective check on spec content. Fires after scenarios stage. Findings auto-applied.
- `bmad-review` (edge-case-hunter lens) — Method-driven branch/boundary walk. Fires after tasks stage.
- `bmad-review` (adversarial lens) — Cynical/red-team review of full spec. Fires after the edge-case-hunter lens.
- `bmad-advanced-elicitation` — Available in `--interactive` mode at per-stage checkpoints `[a]`.
